headline: Sage-Taiyi paper reports metacognitive scientific search and five expert-guided research applications
summary: A Nov. 9 arXiv paper introduces Sage-Taiyi, which links scientific search structures (targets, ideas and evidence) to a monitored cognitive state and reusable methods that select what to investigate next. On the authors’ 265-task Taiyi-Bench, using GPT-5.6-Sol at high reasoning effort, the system reports an overall score of 53.95 versus 47.85 for AI Scientist-v2, the strongest listed baseline. The paper also describes five expert-guided research collaborations; reported outcomes include chemistry model-reaction yields rising from trace to 84% and from 13% to 69%, and a magnesium alloy with mean measured tensile strength of 342 MPa. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced here. The record does not establish that metacognitive components caused the gains, that the benchmark generalizes, or that the results transfer beyond the described tasks and collaborations.
